game_files.label: Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 iOS app (version 1.2.59)
game_files.description: A legally obtained copy of Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 for iOS, version 1.2.59. Extract the .ipa (which is a ZIP archive) and locate the Mach-O executable at Payload/UMK3.app/UMK3. The binary must be the armv7 slice from the fat binary.
game_files.notes: The .ipa file is a ZIP archive. Extract it and use tools/macho.py to thin the armv7 slice from the fat binary. The tools will guide you through extraction of symbols and source tree reconstruction.

first_run: Verify you have a legally obtained copy of Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 for iOS version 1.2.59
The game binary must still contain its STABS debug table (cryptid=0, unstripped); verify this with tools/macho.py
Run the extraction pipeline: python tools/macho.py thin <path/to/UMK3> armv7 work/UMK3.armv7
Dump symbols: python tools/macho.py syms work/UMK3.armv7 work/symbols.txt
Dump functions: python tools/macho.py funcs work/UMK3.armv7 work/functions.txt
Rebuild the source tree from STABS: python tools/stabs.py work/UMK3.armv7 work
Note: This is a work-in-progress decompilation. The project is approximately 74.29% complete. No executable game binary will be produced; only verified C source code and tooling for asset analysis.
notes: This is a decompilation and native port in progress, not a finished game. No playable build exists yet.
The project requires your own legally obtained copy of Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 for iOS version 1.2.59. No game files are distributed.
The binary must be the unstripped armv7 slice with its STABS debug table intact (cryptid=0). This is the only retail build known to have this property.
No game assets (textures, models, audio, game code) are redistributed. All work is reverse engineering and original platform code.

The project uses differential testing against a static ARM-to-C recompiler (tools/armrecomp/recomp.py) as the verification oracle. No function is accepted until it passes this test with zero divergences.

As of the README date, lime/common (109 functions, the portable engine core) is 100% decompiled and verified. gamecode (291 functions) is 100% decompiled. gamecode/logic (the 2,172-function fight engine) is 80.66% decompiled (1,752 functions). The native platform layer (161 functions) is 10% complete.
The original iOS platform layer is not reverse engineered; it is rewritten natively for Windows/Linux.

Two known exceptions: Finch/ (56 functions, OpenAL audio) is a vendored MIT-licensed third-party library; use upstream instead. ROBO1 and ROBO2 are anomalous exports that break several format parsers and require special handling.

game_files.label: Game disc files
game_files.description: Your own copy of Digimon World as a .bin + .cue pair. The .cue file is the small one; the .bin file is the large game data file.
game_files.notes: The port will prompt you to browse for the .cue file on first run. See DISC.md in the repo for exact version requirements and checksums to verify your copy.

first_run: Extract the zip to a location you will keep it, such as C:\Games\Digimon World. Do not run it from inside the zip.
Run Digimon_World_Recompiled.exe. Windows may warn the app is unrecognized; click More info → Run anyway.
Follow the first-run setup. It will offer to download build tools (about 100 MB); leave the box ticked and click Next.
Click Browse Disc and select your .cue file (the small one, not the .bin).
Wait 10–30 minutes while it builds your copy of the game from your disc. This happens only once. It is normal for the launcher to look busy or briefly unresponsive.
Press PLAY. Future launches skip the build and start in seconds.
notes: Controller: plug it in before launching. In the launcher, leave Player 1 on D-Pad. If you switch to Analog, every button stops working—this game only understands the digital controller.
Keyboard: Enter=Start, X=Cross, S=Circle, A=Triangle, Z=Square, arrow keys=D-Pad. Rebind in the launcher's Controls page.
Saving: you can only save by sleeping. Your partner needs the ZZZ bubble over its head, then open the menu and choose Sleep.
Handy keys: F7=save state, F8=rewind, Alt+Enter=fullscreen.
Save states and rewind capture the game as modded. If you take a state with mods on, load it with the same mods on. Use ordinary memory-card saves for the long term.

Widescreen has two known rough edges: for about a second after a wild battle the picture drops back to 4:3 before widening again, and a few interiors were only built as far as the original camera could see, so their edges can be dark (missing scenery on the disc, not a rendering fault).
If the game runs at 4x speed, open the Mods panel and make sure Fast Loading is OFF. It is off by default from 0.1.5 onward.
If you get stuck on the intro movie (runs about two minutes), the Skip all movies cheat is already on by default in cheats.txt and takes you straight to the title.
A save made with Expanded Roster on expects it to stay on. If you turn it off, that save's partner data no longer lines up.

Trigger id collision was fixed in 0.3.4. A save made before this fix may have its recruitment announcements skipped and species raised under the old scheme read as un-raised, but nothing is corrupted.
unsure: Whether the exact USA version/region is required—DISC.md in the repo specifies the required version, but the game_files section does not state a region requirement explicitly.
The exact checksums required for the disc files are stated to be in DISC.md, which this schema does not have access to, so expected_hashes is empty.

mods.notes: Click Mods in the launcher. Sixteen mods are available, all off by default: Expanded Roster (adds 52 raisable Digimon), Trainer (toggles for never hungry/tired/sick/dead, lifespan loss, and training boosts), Perfect Training, Lucky Reels, Training Multiplier (2×–10×), Guaranteed Item Drops, Quality of Life (partner lifespan and world clock speed), Gameplay (tech learning and evolution stat requirements), Widescreen (16:9 or 16:10), Cheats (57 GameShark-style toggles grouped by effect, including infinite HP, freeze clock, max stats, all cards/items), and Fast Loading (off by default and best left off). Turning a mod off restores the original game exactly. A save made with Expanded Roster on expects it to stay on. The Cheats feature can also be controlled via cheats.txt (change [ ] to [x] for any code).

controller_notes: Controller: plug it in before launching. In the launcher, leave the Player 1 toggle on D-Pad. If you switch it to Analog, every button stops working — this game only understands the digital controller, and that is not a bug in the port.
Keyboard: Enter = Start, X = Cross, S = Circle, A = Triangle, Z = Square, arrow keys = D-Pad. Rebind them in the launcher's Controls page.
Handy keys: F7 save state, F8 rewind, Alt+Enter fullscreen.

game_files.notes: The README states the game addresses data by absolute disc sector. You may provide either a raw ISO file or an extracted game/ directory (created via the tools/isoextract.py and tools/cdiextract.py scripts described in the README). The executable will default to game.iso in the current directory if not provided on the command line, or you can set the PSPRECO_ISO environment variable.

game_files.label: Decrypted EBOOT.elf
game_files.description: Your own dumped and decrypted PSP executable from the disc. EBOOT.BIN on the disc is encrypted; you must decrypt it to ELF format using PSP devkit tooling and place it at the repository root.
game_files.notes: This file is required only if you plan to rebuild the recompilation from source. If using the prebuilt release, this file is not needed. The README states: 'Decrypt your own copy to ELF with whatever PSP devkit tooling you already use for that (out of scope here) and place it at the repository root as EBOOT.elf.'

first_run: Extract release.rar to a folder
Extract your disc image (ISO) to a game/ folder using the tools provided, or provide the ISO file directly: python tools/isoextract.py "Ace Combat X.iso" game/
If extracted, optionally unpack the CDI archive for better performance: python tools/cdiextract.py game
Run pspreco-sdl3.exe with the image: pspreco-sdl3.exe generated/image.bin game (or pspreco-sdl3.exe generated/image.bin for game.iso in the current directory)
notes: USA version only (ULUS10176)
The prebuilt release includes generated/image.bin and a compiled pspreco-sdl3.exe; you do not need to recompile
If you wish to rebuild from source, you will need Python 3.10+, clang (or another C11/C++14 compiler), SDL3, and a Vulkan loader
unsure: Whether the prebuilt release's generated/image.bin is included or must be regenerated from EBOOT.elf (the README states it 'deliberately does not ship' it but the release assets do not list separate files)
The exact location where the ISO or extracted game directory should be placed relative to the executable

mods.notes: The Vulkan backend reads PPSSPP-format texture packs. Put the pack's contents (textures.ini and its subdirectories, or a textures.zip) in textures/ULUS10176/ next to the executable, or point PSPRECO_TEXTURES at the directory. Supported formats: png (any colour type and bit depth), dds (DXT1/3/5 and uncompressed 32-bit), and ktx2 (UASTC or ETC1S, with or without Zstandard supercompression). To build a pack, turn on 'Dump textures' under Debug. Every texture the game uploads is written to textures/ULUS10176/new as <hash>.png.

This port is incompatible with the Animal Crossing Deluxe mod due to massive code changes
unsure: The FAQ mentions looking into proper mod support after 1.0 release but doesn't specify the current mod loading mechanism
Exact system requirements (CPU, RAM, GPU) are not documented in the README

mods.notes: Custom textures can be placed in texture_pack/ in Dolphin-compatible format (XXHash64, DDS). HD Texture Pack available at https://forums.dolphin-emu.org/Thread-animal-crossing-hd-texture-pack-version-23-feb-22nd-2026

Keep multiple saves and save often

Whether a Windows build can be produced from source without additional platform-specific dependencies

first_run: Extract the downloaded AlienResurrectionRecompilation-v0.2.0-linux-x64.zip to a folder of your choice
Run the AlienResurrectionLauncher executable
When prompted, select your Alien Resurrection disc image (.cue file). Both the .cue and .bin files must be in the same directory
The launcher will verify the disc is the USA version (serial SLUS-00633)
On first run, the launcher will read the disc, generate C# source code into a local game/ folder, compile it, and then launch the game. This takes time on the first run only
Subsequent runs will reuse the cached compilation and start immediately
notes: This is an early, incomplete release (v0.2.0). Multiple known issues exist: the game can hang on loading screens, progression may be blocked by a door in the airlock section, freezes during level transitions, corrupted 2D graphics on main menu, possible intro video crash on some machines, the game runs about 4% fast, and native resolution must be disabled (it causes a boot hang)

game_files.label: Ape Escape (USA) disc image
game_files.description: A legally obtained Ape Escape (USA, SCUS-94423) disc image in CUE+BIN format. game_files.notes: Must be the USA version (SCUS-94423). Provide both .cue and .bin files together. Do not use cooked/2048-byte .iso format as it loses XA audio/video sectors.

game_files.label: PS1 BIOS (optional retail)
game_files.description: Optionally, a legally obtained retail PS1 BIOS (SCPH1001.BIN). The README states: 'OpenBIOS is selected automatically. Optionally select your legally obtained SCPH1001.BIN in the BIOS row.' OpenBIOS is included in the release, so a retail BIOS is optional.
game_files.notes: Optional. The release includes MIT-licensed OpenBIOS from PCSX-Redux by default. Only provide a retail BIOS if you have one; clear the BIOS row in the launcher to use OpenBIOS.

first_run: Extract ApeEscapeRecomp-v0.3.0-windows-x64.zip to your desired location.
Run ApeEscapeRecomp.exe. A launcher window will open.
In the launcher, the BIOS row shows OpenBIOS selected by default. Optionally select your retail SCPH1001.BIN if you have one.
In the game disc row, select your Ape Escape (USA, SCUS-94423) .cue file (provide both .cue and .bin files in the same folder).
Adjust display options and select any enhancements on the Mods page (Widescreen, Frame Smoothing, Skip FMVs, Quick Gadget Select are bundled).
Press Launch to start the game.
notes: This is a preview build (v0.3.0), not a finished port. Expect rough edges.
The game is playable from intro through gameplay but has not been verified end-to-end to completion.
Ape Escape is a dual-analog title; an analog controller is strongly recommended. Any plugged gamepad is auto-bound as a DualShock.
Save states and rewind are available via launcher hotkeys (F7 for save-state menu, F8 for rewind by default).
The disc image must be in CUE+BIN format, not cooked ISO, to preserve XA sectors for FMV and audio.
Four built-in mods are available: Widescreen (16:9, 21:9, Adaptive), Frame Smoothing (display/120/144/165 Hz blending), Skip FMVs, and Quick Gadget Select.
The launcher saves your disc path, BIOS choice, and options next to the executable.

mods.notes: Four built-in mods are bundled and shown on the Mods page of the launcher: Ape Escape Widescreen (16:9/21:9/Adaptive), Ape Escape Frame Smoothing (temporal blending at display refresh or fixed 120/144/165 Hz), Skip FMVs, and Quick Gadget Select. They are default-off and can be toggled in the launcher before pressing Launch. The mods are located in mods/preloaded/ in the repository source; the release packages them pre-built.

controller_notes: Ape Escape is a dual-analog title — the right stick swings the catch net — so an analog controller is strongly recommended.
Any plugged pad is auto-bound and presented to the game as a DualShock; a keyboard folds onto the analog stick.

game_files.label: Banjo-Kazooie US v1.0 ROM

Run BanjoRecompiled.exe
On the main menu, provide your copy of the North American 1.0 version of Banjo-Kazooie when prompted
Start playing
notes: Requires a GPU supporting Direct3D 12.0 (Shader Model 6), Vulkan 1.2, or Metal Argument Buffers Tier 2
On x86-64 PCs, a CPU supporting SSE4.1 instruction set is required (Intel Core 2 Penryn or AMD Bulldozer and newer)
External framerate limiters (NVIDIA Control Panel, etc.) are known to cause problems; use the in-game graphics menu framerate slider instead
Overlays such as MSI Afterburner and Wallpaper Engine can cause performance issues and should be disabled
Savefiles are stored in %LOCALAPPDATA%\BanjoRecompiled\saves
Can be run in portable mode by placing a file named portable.txt in the same folder as the executable; this will place saves, config, and mods in the same folder as the executable

mods.notes: Mods can be installed by dragging mod files onto the game window before starting the game or by clicking the Install Mods button in the mod menu. Mods can be toggled in the mod menu, and some mods can be configured there. Many mods are available on Thunderstore: https://thunderstore.io/c/banjo-recompiled/. For mod development, see the mod template at https://github.com/BanjoRecomp/BKRecompModTemplate and modding documentation at https://hackmd.io/fMDiGEJ9TBSjomuZZOgzNg. For texture packs, see RT64 documentation at https://github.com/rt64/rt64/blob/main/TEXTURE-PACKS.md.

build_steps: Extract the SLUS_208.51 executable from your Ace Combat 5 NTSC-U disc image (ISO or extracted files)
Verify the executable with: Get-FileHash .\SLUS_208.51 -Algorithm SHA256 (should be C3594227605307806592416DBD723BF5771952E279EE281A40DA305426667385)
Set up MSYS2 PATH in PowerShell: $env:PATH = "C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin;$env:PATH"
Set Python path: $env:PYTHONPATH = "tools"

Run recompiler: python -m ps2recomp "C:\path\to\SLUS_208.51" -o generated --ida-db config/ida_db.json --ida-seeds config/ida_seeds.json --symbols config/sdk_symbols.json --symbols config/manual_symbols.json --overrides config/overrides.json --hooks config/hooks.json
Build with CMake: cmake -S . -B build/gcc -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/gcc.exe -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin/c++.exe
Build: cmake --build build/gcc
required_tools: MSYS2 with GCC 15+ (installed via pacman: mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gcc)

first_run: Install MSYS2 and use pacman to install: mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gcc, mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-sdl3, mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-pkgconf

Copy SDL3.dll and libwinpthread-1.dll from C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin to build/gcc if launching outside a terminal

The MSU-1 mod observes SPC music commands and drives MSU-1 playback: non-looping tracks are Capcom jingle ($00), title screen ($0F), victory jingle ($11), stage selected ($12), got a weapon ($17), and boss tension 1 ($1E). Special SPC commands: $F5 resumes/fades in, $F6 fades out/stops, $FE restores full volume, $FF ducks volume for pause menu.

mods.notes: The texture system works through a folder-based workflow: set a texture folder in settings, enable 'Dump textures while playing' to record which textures the game uses, then press 'Process textures' to upscale them using either Lanczos (built-in) or Real-ESRGAN AI (requires a 43 MB download and Vulkan-capable GPU). The upscaled pack loads automatically on the next launch or when F9 is pressed. Per-stage warming records which textures each chapter uses in <texture folder>/pack/stages/ to fit more of a large pack in the texture cache. Toggle the pack live with F9 while playing to compare. Dumping and using the pack are mutually exclusive (they conflict on the GPU thread). See docs/TEXTURE_PACK.md for full details on the dump/upscale/pack pipeline and file format.

build_steps: Install WSL with Debian or Ubuntu 24.04 on Windows, or use native Linux/macOS

Install build dependencies: make, git, build-essential, binutils-mips-linux-gnu, python3, pip3, libpng-dev (Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt update && sudo apt install make cmake git build-essential binutils-mips-linux-gnu python3 python3-pip clang-format-14 clang-tidy clang-tools)
On macOS: brew update && brew install coreutils make pkg-config tehzz/n64-dev/mips64-elf-binutils
Clone the repository: git clone https://github.com/TheMrIron2/sf64-psp.git
Change into the directory: cd sf64-psp
Install Python dependencies: python3 -m pip install -r ./tools/requirements-python.txt
Update submodules: git submodule update --init --recursive
Build toolchain: make toolchain
Copy your Star Fox 64 US ROM to the root directory and rename it to baserom.us.rev1.z64
Run make init to extract and build
The ROM will be built as build/starfox64.us.rev1.z64
required_tools: WSL (Windows only) with Debian or Ubuntu 24.04

Recompile the game code to C using: python3 tools/recomp/recomp.py game/code/cking.rpx build/gen
Build the project using: cmake -S . -B build/cmake && make -C build/cmake -j$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu) wwhd

game_files.label: Wind Waker HD disc image (USA)
game_files.description: Disc image of The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker HD (USA version) in .wud or .wux format, dumped from your own Wii U disc
game_files.notes: Must be USA version. Extract using tools/wudextract.py

game_files.label: Disc key
game_files.description: The disc key (16 bytes) for your Wind Waker HD disc image, obtained from your own Wii U console
game_files.notes: Place next to the disc image with the same base name (e.g., game.key next to game.wux)

game_files.label: Wii U common key
game_files.description: The Wii U common key (16 raw bytes or 32 hex digits), obtained from your own Wii U console
game_files.notes: Can be placed next to the disc image, in the current directory, or set via WIIU_COMMON_KEY environment variable (32 hex digits)

first_run: Extract the game files by running: python3 tools/wudextract.py game.wux extract game (this creates game/code/cking.rpx, game/content/, and game/meta/)
Recompile the game code by running: python3 tools/recomp/recomp.py game/code/cking.rpx build/gen
Build the native application by running: cmake -S . -B build/cmake && make -C build/cmake -j$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu) wwhd
Launch the game by running: ./build/cmake/wwhd
Saves are stored in the save/ directory
notes: This is a static recompilation for macOS on Apple Silicon only; Windows x64 is not supported
The project requires your own legally obtained Wii U disc and console keys; no game assets or keys are included
Shader caching occurs on first use and is stored in ~/Library/Caches/wwhd/shaders.bin for faster subsequent launches
The game runs at 30 fps (console frame rate) on the TV window; GamePad screen is in a separate window
Optional: Build shader head start for faster launch by recording a template from gameplay, then running tools/shaderprep.py
Frame capture for debugging is available with P or fn+F12, saved to captures/ directory
Known limitations: geometry shaders and rectangle primitives are not yet implemented; shadow edges differ from console; only the opening portion (title, file select, intro, Outset Island) is tested
unsure: Whether later parts of the game beyond Outset Island are fully playable or have compatibility issues
Exact timing behavior during audio initialization that sometimes causes black screen on startup

games.game_title: The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker HD

game_files.label: The Wind Waker HD (USA) dump
game_files.description: Your own dump of the Wii U game: a disc image (.wux or .wud), a Cemu archive (.wua), or an already extracted game folder (with code, content and meta, e.g. from dumpling or Cemu).
game_files.notes: Only the USA version (title 00050000-10143500), version 0 (disc or eShop release, without the update) is supported; setup checks code/cking.rpx against that version's SHA-256. A disc image or .wua is extracted into the release folder (about 1.7 GB); an extracted folder is used where it is. A .wua's bundled update is not used.

game_files.label: Disc key (disc images only)
game_files.description: The 16-byte disc key for your own disc image, as a .key file. Not needed for a Cemu archive or an extracted folder.
game_files.notes: A .key file with the image's name next to the image is used automatically.

game_files.label: Wii U common key (disc images only)
game_files.description: The Wii U common key from your own console (16 bytes, the same on every console). Choose a key file or paste the 32 hex digits. Not needed for a Cemu archive or an extracted folder.
game_files.notes: A common.key next to the image or in the release folder is used automatically. Keys are checked before extraction and never stored.

first_run: Unzip the release anywhere.
Start wind-waker-hd (or Wind Waker HD.desktop; some desktops ask to allow launching it first).
Choose your disc image (plus disc key and common key), Cemu .wua archive, or extracted game folder.
Setup uses your Python 3, downloads the zig compiler (55 MB) into the release folder, then extracts, recompiles and builds the game (about two minutes).
Optionally bring in a save (Cemu/Wii U cking.sav folder, GameCube .gci, or an earlier installation), then start Wind Waker HD to play.
notes: Only the USA version 0 (without the update) is supported.
Needs x86-64 Linux with glibc 2.35 or newer and a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 drivers (or 1.1/1.2 with VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering).
Everything (built game, extracted game files, saves in data/save, settings and save states in data/user, crash logs) stays in the release folder's data/ folder.
To repair, update or change the game, start it with --setup (or the Setup action of its menu entry).
Status: the opening of the game is tested and matches Cemu; later parts are untested. Startup can sit on a black screen for up to a minute before the logo.
Settings overlay: F1, or hold Select / press Home on a controller. F11 or Alt+Enter toggles full screen.
unsure: A newer release (v0.2.2) exists; the catalog tag v0.2.1 is used.

mods.notes: Optional gameplay mods (Gameplay menu, all off by default): climb any wall, direct right-stick camera, mouse camera, first person on the mouse wheel, quick doors, fast scene changes. Also available in the settings overlay along with cheats.

first_run: Unzip the release anywhere.
Open Wind Waker HD.app. It isn't signed by Apple: on macOS 14 right-click the app, Open, Open; on macOS 15+ click Done, then System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway.
If Apple's Command Line Tools are missing, accept the installer it offers.

To repair, update or change the game, hold Shift while starting it.
Status: the opening of the game is tested and matches Cemu; later parts are untested. Startup can sit on a black screen for up to a minute before the logo.
The macOS app does not drive controller rumble yet. Settings overlay: F1 (Fn+F1 on most Mac keyboards) or Cmd+,.

mods.notes: Optional gameplay mods (Gameplay menu, all off by default): climb any wall, direct right-stick camera, mouse camera, first person on the mouse wheel, quick doors, fast scene changes. Also available in the settings overlay along with cheats.

controller_notes: Game controllers (Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro, MFi) work too; buttons map by position.

The Input menu switches whether keyboard and controllers act as the Wii U GamePad (default) or as a Wii U Pro Controller (WWHD_PRO_CONTROLLER=1 starts in that mode); with the Pro Controller, the GamePad window keeps its screen and touch input.
When the game asks for text (e.g. your name), a macOS text field opens.

build_steps: Install Python 3.10+ with the py launcher
Install capstone 5.x via 'py -3 -m pip install --user capstone'
Install Git for Windows (includes Git Bash)
Install CMake 3.20 or newer
Install Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools with 'Desktop development with C++'
Clone xboxrecomp beside the burnout3 folder: 'git clone https://github.com/sp00nznet/xboxrecomp' and 'git clone https://github.com/sp00nznet/burnout3'

Unpack your disc image into 'burnout3\Burnout 3 Takedown\' using: 'cd xboxrecomp && py -3 -m tools.xiso unpack "path\to\Burnout 3 - Takedown (USA).iso" -o "..\burnout3\Burnout 3 Takedown" && cd ..\burnout3'
Regenerate the C code in Git Bash: './regen.sh --disasm'
Build with CMake: 'cmake -S . -B build-xr -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64'
Build the executable: 'cmake --build build-xr --config Release --parallel 2'
Run from the repo folder: '.\bin\burnout3.exe'
required_tools: Python 3.10 or newer with py launcher
Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools with Desktop development with C++

build_steps: Clone the repository: git clone https://github.com/BlackAndBlue95/Strikers-WiiCompiled.git
Install the build tools for your platform (see the wiki's Building page).
Run build.cmd from the repository folder and pick your Mario Strikers Charged (USA, Rev 1, R4QE01) disc image when asked.
The script extracts the disc, translates the game code and compiles the runtime; the game files, config, saves and caches end up in an MSCRecomp folder.

game_files.label: Mario Strikers Charged disc image (USA, Rev 1, R4QE01)
game_files.description: Your own legally dumped disc image of Mario Strikers Charged, USA, Rev 1 (R4QE01).
game_files.notes: The build script asks you to pick the disc image, extracts it, and checks main.dol's SHA-256, rejecting any other version. The disc image isn't needed after the build.

first_run: After the build finishes, launch the compiled game.
Press F10 to open the settings (graphics, frame rate, controls, Wii Remotes, tweaks and mods).
notes: Early, work-in-progress port developed and tested on macOS (Apple Silicon); Windows and Linux builds use the same toolchain but are untested with this port.
There are no prebuilt releases.
Only the USA Rev 1 disc (R4QE01) is mapped; other regions and revisions won't work. Online play and WiiConnect24 aren't supported.
Needs a 64-bit OS (Windows 10/11, Linux, or macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon), a GPU with Direct3D 12, Vulkan or Metal, and about 10 GB of free disk space.

GameCube controllers work through the official Wii U / Switch GameCube adapter (on Windows, switch it to the WinUSB driver once with Zadig). Real Wii Remotes are supported experimentally over Bluetooth.
unsure: The exact per-platform setup is on the wiki's Building page, which isn't included in the job text.
The name and location of the compiled executable and the MSCRecomp folder aren't stated in the README.
Accepted disc image formats aren't stated.
The expected main.dol SHA-256 value isn't published in the README.

games.game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

build_steps: Install Python 3.10 (add it to PATH during install), Git (x64 build) and Visual Studio Community 2022 with C++ development.
Clone the repo with submodules: git clone --recursive https://github.com/blawar/ooot.git, then cd ooot.
Put your ROM as baserom_original.z64 (or .n64) in roms\PAL_1.0\ (EUR PAL 1.0 retail) or roms\EUR_MQD\ (EUR Master Quest Debug).
Extract the assets: python setup.py -b PAL_1.0 (or python setup.py -b EUR_MQD).
Open OOT.sln from the vs folder, select Debug - Win32 or Release - Win32, right-click oot and click Build.

game_files.label: Ocarina of Time ROM (EUR PAL 1.0 retail)
game_files.description: The EUR PAL 1.0 retail ROM dumped from your own copy of the game. Needed to extract the game's assets before building.
game_files.notes: Use this OR the EUR Master Quest Debug ROM. Named baserom_original.z64 or baserom_original.n64. If the ROM's hash is not correct, setup.py won't extract the assets.

game_files.label: Ocarina of Time Master Quest Debug ROM (EUR)
game_files.description: The EUR Master Quest Debug ROM from your own copy. An alternative to the PAL 1.0 retail ROM for extracting the assets.
game_files.notes: Use this OR the PAL 1.0 retail ROM. Named baserom_original.z64 or baserom_original.n64. If the ROM's hash is not correct, setup.py won't extract the assets.

first_run: Build the project in Visual Studio (Win32 configuration) after extracting assets with setup.py.
Run the built oot program.
notes: Only the 32-bit x86/Win32 build is supported, with Visual Studio 2019 or newer.
You must use the ZAPD included with this repository, not the main ZAPD branch.
Clone with --recursive so the submodules come along.

Higher frame rates (30/60/120 FPS) are on the dev branch: git checkout dev, git pull origin dev, git submodule update --init --recursive, then rerun setup.py and build. In game, F7 goes back to 20 FPS and F8 steps up.
F9 toggles language (English, German, French).
Settings such as cheats, Owl prompts and control inversion are in config.json.
unsure: The README gives two different MD5s for the PAL 1.0 ROM (9526b263... near the top and c02c1d79... in the setup section); which one applies to .z64 vs .n64 isn't stated.
The name and location of the built executable aren't stated.
Where texture packs go isn't stated.

mods.notes: Ability to load high resolution GLideN64 texture packs such as oot-reloaded (https://evilgames.eu/texture-packs/oot-reloaded.htm).

controller_notes: Right joystick free camera control (can be disabled)
Controller rumble support.
Pause menu keyboard/gamepad rebind screen.

game_files.label: Dance Dance Revolution (Japan) disc dump
game_files.description: A Redump-style dump of your own Dance Dance Revolution (Japan) disc, SLPM-86222: one .cue plus 40 .bin tracks (track 1 is data, 2-40 are the CDDA music). The setup-host asks for the disc and generates and compiles the game from it.
game_files.notes: Reference dump: Track 01 .bin is 14,935,200 bytes, md5 57d6ae6568a77409abfc94ba1d695b62. A wrong dump is refused. A different revision may still work, but the fixes were derived from this one.

first_run: Unzip ddr1st-0.4.0-windows-x64.zip and run it.
Point it at your own Dance Dance Revolution (Japan) .cue when asked; it generates and compiles the game on your machine (first run takes minutes).
Later runs start immediately; settings.toml is written beside the executable.
notes: The release is a setup-host, not a ready-made game: it builds the recompiled executable from your own disc.
The random hard-freeze is contained (not fully cured) by the runtime.
The README says publishing the setup-host zip had not yet been exercised from this repository when it was written.
unsure: The setup-host executable name and exact launch steps are not documented in the README.
Whether the setup-host needs extra tools (Python, CMake/Clang toolchain) on the user's machine is not stated for the release zip.

game_files.label: PlayStation Doom disc image (.cue)
game_files.description: A disc image of PlayStation Doom from a disc you own, as a '.cue' file plus the disc data it describes. Final Doom, the Doom single level demo disc and GEC Master Edition Beta 3 or 4 are also supported.
game_files.notes: A valid .cue file must be provided before launching; it can be specified on launch with -cue <CUE_FILE_PATH>. All regions and editions of Doom and Final Doom are supported.

first_run: Make the AppImage executable and run it.
Provide your Doom .cue file (e.g. run with -cue <CUE_FILE_PATH>).
notes: Supported Linux versions are Debian 'Buster' based distros or later; others may work but are untested. PulseAudio is needed for sound.
One build runs both PlayStation Doom and Final Doom (all regions & editions) - supply whichever disc you own.
The Vulkan renderer (widescreen & high resolutions) needs a Vulkan 1.0 capable GPU (Metal on macOS); it is enabled by default where supported.
For the best audio quality set your audio device's sample rate to 44.1 kHz.
Link-cable multiplayer is emulated over TCP (default port 666 on Windows and macOS, 1666 on Linux) and needs a very low latency connection.
Pass -nolauncher (or any other command line argument) to skip the launcher.
This is a preview build (1.2.0-preview1); the latest stable release is releases/1.1.1.
unsure: The README does not say whether the launcher has a file picker for the .cue file; only the -cue command line argument is documented.

mods.notes: User mods are supplied in the form of a directory. Specify where the mod directory is located using launcher or via the `-datadir <MY_DIRECTORY_PATH>` command line argument. Extra IWADs can be added with `-file <WAD_FILE_PATH>`.

game_files.label: Quest 64 ROM (USA)
game_files.description: The original USA Quest 64 ROM dumped from your own cartridge. Select it in the launcher.
game_files.notes: USA ROM only. The SHA-1 is for the big-endian ROM; the launcher accepts standard N64 ROM byte orders.

first_run: Extract the ZIP and run Quest64Recompiled.
Select your USA ROM in the launcher, then start the game.
Configure graphics, input bindings and mods in Settings.
notes: Needs x86-64 Linux with Vulkan support plus SDL2, GTK 3, zlib, X11 and compatible C/C++ system libraries. The Linux release uses Ubuntu's system libraries; it is not a self-contained AppImage.
Saving while stat-boost packs are active records the boosted values; use a separate save slot for experiments.
Newer releases (v1.0.8, v1.0.9) add camera-relative movement, 16:9 HUD placement and the Solvaring Backstory FMV pack support.

mods.notes: Download the packs from the separate mods repository (https://github.com/boricuapab/quest64tale-recompiled-mods). Open the launcher Mods tab, choose Open Mods Folder, copy the packs there and enable them. Mods in this project's custom .qsmod format require this application's compiled handlers. New gameplay packs require v1.0.7.

build_steps: Clone the repository.
Extract and decrypt the files listed in yakuza/REGENERATE.md from your own copy of the game (e.g. game\EBOOT.elf and game\ogrez_shader_ps3.ppu.elf).
py -3 tools\find_functions.py game\EBOOT.elf -o functions.json
py -3 tools\ppu_lifter.py game\EBOOT.elf --output recomp\ --functions functions.json --override-funcs yakuza\movie_overrides.txt
py -3 tools\lift_prx.py game\ogrez_shader_ps3.ppu.elf --base 0x02200000 --output recomp_prx\

py -3 tools\ppu_lifter.py recomp_prx\ogrez_shader_ps3.ppu_image.bin --raw --base 0x02200000 --functions recomp_prx\ogrez_shader_ps3.ppu_functions.json --output recomp\prx --header-name pxd_shader_recomp.h --source-name pxd_shader_recomp --table-name pxd_shader_function_table --extern-funcs recomp\ppu_recomp.h
py -3 tools\gen_spu_images.py
From a Visual Studio x64 developer prompt: cd yakuza, then cmake --preset release, then cmake --build --preset release, then cd ..
required_tools: Visual Studio 2022 or newer with the C++ workload
FFmpeg development package (optional, for movies; third_party/ffmpeg or -DYZ_FFMPEG_DIR=<path>)

first_run: Run the exe. Windows SmartScreen will flag it because it is unsigned: click "More info" then "Run anyway".

notes: LegoToypad is not a game port: it is a companion app that emulates the LEGO Dimensions Toypad and every tag (75 characters, 240 vehicles, 30 franchises) and sends them to an emulator.

It needs an emulator build with the Toypad listener enabled: Cemu-2.6-Remote-Toypad-Build (harrysof), RPCS3-Seamless-Toypad-Build (NeverCookFirst), shadPS4-Seamless-Toypad-Build (harrysof/shadPS4) or Xenia-Seamless-Toypad-Build (NeverCookFirst).
Everything (tags, art, sounds) is baked into the exe; there are no loose files to manage.
It also works with the recompiled PC port (legodimensions.exe): the picker opens on the game's monitor and returns focus to it.
The sneak peek overlay needs the emulator running in windowed or borderless mode.
unsure: The game itself (LEGO Dimensions) and the emulator are supplied and set up separately; this app needs no game files of its own.

LEGO Dimensions shipped on several consoles; the app supports Cemu (Wii U), RPCS3 (PS3), shadPS4 (PS4) and Xenia (Xbox 360) builds, so the console listed here is only the primary one named in the description.

game_files.label: Revenge of the Sith Xbox disc image (North America)
game_files.description: Your own disc image of Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith for the original Xbox, North American release: an .iso (XISO or a full Redump-style image), or a .7z/.zip/.rar archive containing one. On first run swrots.exe asks for it, checks it is the supported release, and copies the game files into GameData\ (about 2.5 GB).
game_files.notes: The game's executable (default.xbe) must have MD5 6460ef37862de3af364a0563a0a18c4e - this is the hash of the executable inside the disc, not of the image file. Archives are unpacked with Windows' built-in tar (Windows 10 1803+); if that fails, unpack it yourself and choose the .iso. `swrots.exe --install <image>` skips the file dialog.

first_run: Unpack swrots.exe and core.dll from the zip into a folder of your choice, e.g. C:\Games\SWROTS.
Run swrots.exe. The first time, it asks for your disc image (.iso/.xiso, or a .7z/.zip/.rar containing one), checks it, copies the game files into GameData\ and adds a Start menu shortcut.
Play. Settings are in settings.ini and key bindings in controls.ini, both next to swrots.exe.
notes: Status: early development. Playable through level changes, restarts and saving, but not yet played through from start to finish; expect bugs.
Only the North American release is supported.
Requires 64-bit Windows 10 (1803) or newer and a Direct3D 9 capable graphics card (the port itself is a 32-bit program).
60 fps (FpsLimit=60) is experimental: some of the game's logic is timed for 30 fps.
The keyboard and the first controller are both player 1; two-player modes need two controllers. Controllers other than Xbox (XInput) and PlayStation need Steam Input or a similar translator.
To reinstall, delete the GameData folder; saves, settings and mods are kept.
unsure: The zip's exact contents beyond swrots.exe and core.dll are not listed.

mods.notes: Mods as loose files: replace textures, models and other game files without rebuilding archives. `mods\` overrides any disc file. Variables can be set at every start in `mods\vars_xbox.cfg` (`name=value`, one per line). Your own meshes go under `mods\meshes\chars\<folder>\` with their textures. Some limits: animations stored in a level's memory image (most `.bnm`) cannot be replaced by loose files yet, and loose text resources in folders the disc also has (e.g. `gameinfo\`) fail to load.

build_steps: Clone https://github.com/NagyD/SDLPoP.

Download the SDL2 and SDL2_image Visual C++ development packages (the *-VC.zip files) from https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/releases/latest and https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL_image/releases/latest.
Copy the SDL2_image folder contents into the SDL2 folder so their DLLs and headers sit in the same place.
Open a command prompt and run Visual Studio's vcvarsall.bat with 'x64' as the parameter.
Set the SDL2 environment variable to that folder, e.g. set "SDL2=C:\libraries\SDL2-2.0.8".
Run build.bat in the src/ directory.
Add the SDL2 / SDL2_image DLL folder to PATH so the built executable can find them, then double-click prince.exe.

first_run: Double-click prince.exe (open a command line if you want to pass options such as 'full' for full screen).
Press Esc or Backspace for the in-game menu; Alt+Enter toggles full screen.
notes: The repository includes the game's data folder, so no separate game files are needed.
Alternatives to Visual Studio: Dev-C++ with the SDL2 MinGW libraries (open a .dev file and compile), MSVC with NMake (src/NMakefile), or CMake with MinGW-w64.
Prebuilt Windows versions are offered off GitHub at https://www.popot.org/get_the_games.php?game=SDLPoP.
Saves (SAV) and hall-of-fame (HOF) files go to the folder in SDLPOP_SAVE_PATH if that environment variable is set.
Gameplay bug fixes can be turned off with use_fixes_and_enhancements=false in SDLPoP.ini, or in the in-game settings menu (GAMEPLAY > Enhanced mode).
unsure: There are no GitHub releases; the README's compiled versions are hosted on popot.org.
The README's Visual Studio example uses 'x86'; that x64 builds work the same way is implied ('either x86 or x64') but not shown.

mods.notes: Since version 1.17, the game can also load from mod folders that have been placed in the "mods/" directory; only the files different from the original V1.0 data are required. Choose the mod by setting 'levelset' in SDLPoP.ini to the mod's folder name, or run `prince mod "Mod Name"`. Mods can also include a mod.ini and music in mods/<modname>/music. Example mod: https://forum.princed.org/viewtopic.php?f=73&t=3664 (alternate: https://www.popot.org/custom_levels.php?mod=0000153).

controller_notes: Joystick: left/right (for all-directional joystick movement, set joystick_only_horizontal to false in SDLPoP.ini)
If SDLPoP does not work correctly with your gamepad, it might help if you download gamecontrollerdb.txt and configure SDLPoP to use it.

build_steps: Install MSYS2 (msys2-x86_64-latest.exe) to C:\dev\msys64 and run it.
In the MSYS2 shell run: pacman -Syuu. Then open "MSYS2 MinGW 64-Bit" and run pacman -Syuu repeatedly until there are no more updates.
Install the toolchain: pacman -S --needed base-devel mingw-w64-i686-toolchain mingw-w64-x86_64-toolchain git subversion mercurial mingw-w64-i686-cmake mingw-w64-x86_64-cmake
Install dependencies: pacman -S mingw-w64-i686-glew mingw-w64-x86_64-glew mingw-w64-i686-SDL2 mingw-w64-x86_64-SDL2 python3
Clone the repository into a folder under C:\msys64\home\<username>\.
Copy your ROM into the repository root named baserom.us.z64.
cd tools/audiofile-0.3.6/ and run: autoreconf -i
Run: PATH=/mingw64/bin:/mingw32/bin:$PATH LIBS=-lstdc++ ./configure --disable-docs
Run: PATH=/mingw64/bin:/mingw32/bin:$PATH make
Run: mkdir ../lib, then cp libaudiofile/.libs/libaudiofile.a ../lib/ and cp libaudiofile/.libs/libaudiofile.la ../lib/
Edit tools/Makefile: change the line tabledesign_CFLAGS := -Wno-uninitialized -laudiofile to end with -lstdc++ (tabledesign_CFLAGS := -Wno-uninitialized -laudiofile -lstdc++).
cd .. and run: PATH=/mingw64/bin:/mingw32/bin:$PATH make
cd .. back to the repository root and run make, adding any options you want, e.g. PATH=/mingw32/bin:/mingw64/bin:$PATH make BETTERCAMERA=1 NODRAWINGDISTANCE=1
The .exe is produced under build\ (build/us_pc for the US version).

build_steps: Install Xcode Command Line Tools with: xcode-select --install
Install Homebrew and build dependencies with: brew install cmake ninja sdl2 ffmpeg glslang spirv-cross nlohmann-json python
Clone the repository: git clone https://github.com/Sean13128/disgaea-d2-recomp.git && cd disgaea-d2-recomp
Set up Python virtual environment: python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r tools/requirements-lifts.txt
Bootstrap the SDK: ./tools/bootstrap_sdk.sh "$PWD/ps3recomp"
Decrypt your game executable with RPCS3 (File → Install Packages/Raps/Edats for 1.40 update and DLC, then Utilities → Decrypt PS3 Binaries on the EBOOT.BIN files)
Copy decrypted 1.40 EBOOT.elf to work/v140/EBOOT.elf (or work/EBOOT.elf for 1.00 version)
Generate lift code for version 1.40: PYTHON="$PWD/.venv/bin/python" ./tools/generate_lifts.sh --version 140

Configure CMake build: cmake -S port -B port/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DPS3RECOMP_DIR=../ps3recomp -DD2_GAME_VERSION=140 -DPython3_EXECUTABLE="$PWD/.venv/bin/python" -DCMAKE_{C,CXX,OBJC,OBJCXX}_FLAGS=-I/opt/homebrew/include
Build the app: cmake --build port/build --target DisgaeaD2Dist
Run the app: open "port/dist/Disgaea D2.app"

first_run: Make the setup executable (chmod +x P.T.PC.Port.Setup-linux) and run it from a terminal.
Point it at your dump folder or fake PKG and at a destination folder; it copies the three game archives next to the port.
Start pt from the install folder (or the menu entry the setup creates).
Have a microphone ready for one part of the game, or set key = J under [voice] in pt.ini to use a key instead.
notes: Needs Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.38 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 39, current Arch and SteamOS) and a Vulkan 1.3 GPU/driver.
FSR, DLSS and XeSS upscalers are Windows-only and are left out of the Linux build.
On Steam Deck install from desktop mode and add pt as a non-Steam game.
Settings, save, pt.log and crash dumps go to ~/.local/share/pt-port/pt/.
The game checks the Releases page for a newer version at start; [network] check_updates = 0 in pt.ini turns that off.

first_run: Extract the release and place zelda3.sfc (or zelda3.smc) next to the game.

notes: Only the USA ROM is supported for normal extraction; localized ROMs are only used to add extra dialogue languages.
The executable tries zelda3.user.ini first, then falls back to zelda3.ini; put personal settings in zelda3.user.ini.
If you move the executable, copy zelda3.ini and zelda3_assets.dat beside it.
PCM MSU packs expect AudioFreq = 44100; OPUZ packs expect AudioFreq = 48000.
The release also offers Z3R-linux-x64.tar.gz and a Flatpak (Z3R-linux.flatpak).
unsure: The README only documents building from source; it does not say whether the release packages include the Python asset scripts or how they produce zelda3_assets.dat.

notes: Only the USA ROM is supported for normal extraction; localized ROMs are only used to add extra dialogue languages.
The executable tries zelda3.user.ini first, then falls back to zelda3.ini; put personal settings in zelda3.user.ini.
If you move the executable, copy zelda3.ini and zelda3_assets.dat beside it.
PCM MSU packs expect AudioFreq = 44100; OPUZ packs expect AudioFreq = 48000.
README troubleshooting: launch it from the project root or from bin\x64-Release\.
unsure: The README only documents building from source; it does not say whether the release packages include the Python asset scripts or how they produce zelda3_assets.dat.
The exact folder the ROM must go in for the prebuilt release is not stated (README says the project root).
The executable name inside the release package is not stated.
No ROM checksum is published in the README.

mods.notes: LinkGraphics: path to a .zspr Link sprite file. Shader: path to a .glsl or .glslp shader. Shaders require OpenGL. EnableMSU: false, true, deluxe, opuz, or deluxe-opuz. MSUPath: prefix for MSU files. The track number and extension are appended.

controller_notes: `[KeyMap]` binds keyboard keys. The `Controls` order is:
Up, Down, Left, Right, Select, Start, A, B, X, Y, L, R
`[GamepadMap]` uses button names such as `DpadUp`, `DpadDown`, `Back`, `Start`, `A`, `B`, `X`, `Y`, `L1`, `R1`, `Lb`, `Rb`, `L2`, and `R2`.
